question.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}-24x+{y}^{2}+6y=-137.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-24x+{y}^{2}+6y & =-137 \\ ({x}^{2}-24x)+({y}^{2}+6y) & =-137 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 12x+{12}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 3y+{3}^{2}) & =-137+{12}^{2}+{3}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 12x+{12}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot 3y+{3}^{2}) & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-12)^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & ={4}^{2} \\ (x-12)^{2}+(y-(-3))^{2} & ={4}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(12,-3)$ and its radius is $4.$
